personas.name: Nia Okafor
personas.story: I funded a 240-page risograph art book on my own, at my kitchen table, and I still cannot believe 420 people gave me money for it. The printer moved my slot twice and now I open Kickstarter every morning with my stomach in a knot. I answer every single message myself, at night, after my day job, and I have started to dread the little red dot.
personas.dataReceived: Kickstarter backer report CSV only (no KS API exists). Tideover receives: Backer Number, Backer Name, Email, Reward Title, Reward Minimum, Pledge Amount, Pledged Status, Shipping Country. POPULATED: email, firstName, orderValueCents, sourceKey->importKey, group=ks-backer. MISSING: no Estimated Delivery column exists, so disclosedEta is undefined for all 420 orders (every one lands in dispute-exposure unknownCount and the evidence pack has no 'we disclosed X' artifact). Pledge-date header name is inconsistent across KS exports (Highview Apps: 'There is not a consistent set of column names in the Kickstarter CSV file'), so the datelessRows counter is the load-bearing signal on day 0. region hardcoded 'US' even though Shipping Country is in the file. ltvCents = summed pledge value, not lifetime value.

intake.voice: A tired, warm, one-person studio. Writes like a person, not a brand. Explains what is physically happening in the print shop and never guesses at a date.

No repeat orders exist yet, so every ltvCents sits far below the hardcoded $500 high tier - the LTV gate is dead weight here and priority must come from risk band, not money. SIMULATED population.

events.subject: CSV import: 420 backers, day 52 of the wait
events.body: Kickstarter backer report exported this morning and dropped into Tideover.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Run the import and read the datelessRows counter before anything else. If the export's date header missed the aliases, all 420 rows read day 0 and every wait clock, band, and confidence range in the product is wrong. Re-export or set fulfillmentStart by hand, then confirm disclosedEta is undefined for the whole file and accept that the evidence pack has no disclosure artifact for this campaign.

events.subject: Just checking in, no rush
events.body: Hi Nia, not chasing, just curious how the book is going. I have been quiet on the updates because I figured you would post when there was something to post. Hope the printing is going well.
events.expectedOperatorAction: This is the reassurance-class backer - loyal, quiet, invisible to any queue sorted by anger or volume. Approve the deterministic draft with the current stage blurb and the confidence band. Cheapest ticket in the queue to keep, most expensive to ignore.

events.subject: Update?
events.body: There has been no update since the middle of May and no reply to the message I sent two weeks ago. I am not trying to be difficult but the silence is loud.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Note the grievance is the non-reply, not the delay. Approve a draft that names the last update, states the current stage, and gives the band. Do not apologise in the abstract; answer the actual complaint.

events.subject: Moved house
events.body: I have moved since I backed. New address below. I updated it on Kickstarter too but I have no idea if that actually goes anywhere.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Log the address change against the order. Do not trust the Kickstarter address-update email as the system of record; half of them show no change when you open the spreadsheet. Confirm back in writing so the backer stops asking.

events.subject: Refund
events.body: I backed this in February. It is July. I would like my money back rather than wait another three months for a book I will have stopped caring about.
events.expectedOperatorAction: High-value tier backer. Score the refund risk, offer the mid-tier goodwill gift with the stage detail, and never counter with a date. If they hold, log the save in the outcome ledger; if they still want out, refund cleanly and record it.

events.subject: Press slot moved three weeks
events.body: Broadcast: the printer lost my press slot to a bigger job. Interior pages move about three weeks later than the last band I gave.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Widen the window band on the status page BEFORE posting, push the update, and expect the wave. The band moves; no new hard date is issued. Watch the WISMO cohort forecast for the next 72 hours.

events.subject: Comment wall spike after the delay post
events.body: Public campaign comments, 40+ in six hours. Top comment: 'Another push back. I gave you kind views on the last two delays. This is over the top now.' Reply chain is other backers agreeing.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Answer in public, once, with the band and the stage. Serve the many rather than one at a time. Do not go quiet - the silence after a delay post is what converts backers into detractors. Approve one public-facing reply and let the status page absorb the rest.

events.subject: Re: Update?
events.body: So the answer is another delay. Cool. At what point does this stop being a delay and start being a pattern?
events.expectedOperatorAction: Second contact from the same backer, tone escalated. Risk band should have moved. Reply with the specific stage and what physically changed, not with reassurance language.

events.subject: Re: Refund
events.body: No reply to my refund request either. That is what actually bothers me now. Not the book. The fact that nobody answers.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Silence on a refund request is its own grievance. Escalate to the top of the queue, reply same day, and start the evidence pack: pledge date, every update posted, every reply sent.

events.subject: Shipping to Canada?
events.body: Is Canada in the same shipping wave as the US or do we go later? Last campaign I backed, we went two months later and nobody said so up front.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Region is hardcoded 'US' at import even though the KS export carries Shipping Country. Fix the region on this order by hand or the status page tells a Canadian backer a US story. Answer with the wave logic, published.

events.subject: Was I charged twice?
events.body: I see two charges from Kickstarter on my card. Did something go wrong with my pledge?
events.expectedOperatorAction: Money question, not a wait question. Answer factually from the pledge record and resolve fast - unanswered money questions become disputes at a much higher rate than unanswered wait questions.

events.subject: Saw the update, thanks
events.body: Thanks for actually explaining what happened with the press. I would rather have that than a fake date.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Close it, log a CSAT, and note in the ledger that the delay post plus band retained a standard-band backer. This is the evidence the proof pack is built from.

events.subject: Add a second copy?
events.body: Can I add another copy for a friend and pay you directly? I do not want to miss the run.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Revenue the merchant would otherwise refuse and convert into a ticket. Handle it as a late-pledge, tag the order, and do not let it queue behind WISMO.

events.subject: Where is it
events.body: Any actual movement, or is this the part where the updates stop for three months?
events.expectedOperatorAction: Third contact. Band should be at_risk. Approve a draft with a full-tier goodwill unlock and a specific stage fact. The pattern to break is: creator goes quiet after a delay, backer escalates.

events.subject: Filing with my bank
events.body: I am giving you until Friday and then I am calling my card company. I have asked three times.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Pull the evidence pack now: pledge date, every update posted, every reply sent, the stage timeline. Reply the same day. Decide refund versus save on the ledger, not on mood.

events.subject: Sorry to add to the pile
events.body: I know you are getting a lot of these. Just wanted to say I am still in and the book will be worth it.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Low-effort approve. Log CSAT. The queue's emotional read of the campaign is set by the 1% who shout; this ticket is the counterweight and belongs in the outcome ledger.

events.subject: Cohort question
events.body: What batch am I in? Backer number 260, if that helps.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Answer from the wave, not from a spreadsheet lookup. If this ticket still requires opening a spreadsheet to answer, the import did not work.

personas.withoutTideover: Gmail plus one Google Sheet of the KS backer export, sorted by backer number. Every WISMO is a manual query against that sheet. At the merchant-reported handling time of 5-10 minutes per WISMO ticket (Shopify Community, abhishek27377), and roughly 8-14 tickets a day across a 420-backer campaign in a delay window, that is 0.7-2.3 hours/day of lookup-and-reply - a SIMULATED formula-based estimate from stated assumptions, not a measured result. What slips: the delay post gets written three times and posted late because she is afraid of the comment wall; the refund request at index 88 sits unanswered for eleven days and turns into a chargeback threat; the address change at index 3 is logged in a sheet and never reaches the packing list.

personas.name: Priya Raghunathan
personas.story: We raised on Kickstarter for a modular desk light and 18,400 people backed it, which is roughly 18,000 more than we planned for. The tooling vendor cracked a mould in the second shot and the whole thing moved by eight weeks. We have two people answering messages and the comments section has decided we are a scam.
personas.dataReceived: Kickstarter native Pledge Manager export CSV. Tideover receives the backer-report fields plus add-ons, shipping paid, taxes paid, PM status, survey timestamps, and per-SKU columns. POPULATED: email, firstName, orderValueCents, sourceKey, group, and a real pledge date if the header hits an alias. The PM amount aliases are defensive guesses; no primary source publishes the column spec. No estimated-delivery column, so disclosedEta is undefined for all 18,400 orders.

events.expectedOperatorAction: Widen the band on the status page first, then post with the photo of the cracked tool. Send the cohort a status link. Expect the WISMO forecast to spike for 5-7 days and staff for it.

This is the moment morale collapses and creators stop posting - the status page exists so the merchant does not have to win an argument to stay visible.

events.subject: Refund, all of it
events.body: Eight weeks becomes twelve, then it becomes a year. Refund my pledge and my add-ons.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Look at the true value including add-ons, not the imported number. This is a high-value backer wearing a standard-tier badge because the importer dropped $220 of add-ons. Unlock the full-tier gift manually if the band does not do it, and start the evidence pack.

events.subject: It is fine
events.body: Five months late is normal for this kind of thing. Just keep posting.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Baseline tolerance is high. Approve, log, move on - and read it as confirmation that update cadence, not speed, is the product.

events.subject: Address change - moved countries
events.body: I have moved from Germany to Ireland since backing. Does that change my wave?
events.expectedOperatorAction: Address change that also changes the freight cohort. Log both. Region matters here because EU hub timing differs from US.

events.subject: Two questions
events.body: Hi. When will it actually SHIP, not when will it arrive. Those are different questions and the updates keep answering the second one.
events.expectedOperatorAction: The question is about the pre-label period. Answer the ship band, not the delivery band. Every tracking tool in the market is blind to this window, which is precisely why the ticket exists.

events.subject: Add-on payment
events.body: I paid an extra $180 in the pledge manager for the wall mounts. Is that recorded anywhere? It does not show on anything you have sent me.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Tideover did not persist the add-on. Answer from the pledge manager, not from Tideover, and flag the gap. Do not let the customer status page contradict what they paid.

events.subject: Cancel
events.body: By the time this ships the tech will have moved on. That happened to me with a drone campaign and I am not doing it twice.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Delivery-window obsolescence. Reassurance about the wait will not land; the fear is about the product's value at delivery. Counter with what the spec still does, offer the mid-tier gift, log the outcome either way.

events.subject: Re: Wave question
events.body: Thanks for publishing the batch order. First campaign that has actually told me where I am in the queue.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Close, log CSAT, and note in the ledger that publishing the wave logic reduced repeat WISMO from this cohort. That is a measurable deflection claim, sourced from the ledger, not asserted.

events.subject: VIP: our reviewer copy
events.body: This is Marcus at a tech publication. We were promised an early unit for review and our slot is now closed. What is happening?
events.expectedOperatorAction: VIP escalation with reach. Route to the founder, not the queue. Do not send a templated reply. Log it as an escalation in the ledger with the reply the founder actually sent.

events.subject: You have gone quiet again
events.body: Two weeks since the tooling post. Backers count the gap in months and we do notice.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Cadence is being audited by the crowd. Ship a short stage update even when nothing has changed. 'Nothing changed, here is why' is a valid update; silence is not.

events.subject: Chargeback filed
events.body: Filed with my card issuer. Two months, no product, a delay announcement, and a reply that took six days.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Generate the evidence pack: pledge date, every update posted, reply timestamps, stage timeline, the band that was disclosed and when. Note the missing artifact: no disclosedEta exists on this import, so there is no 'we disclosed X' record - that gap is the cost of the KS export having no delivery column.

events.subject: Batch 3 or batch 4
events.body: Simple question, which batch. It is my third time asking.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Third ask means the first two answers did not reach them or did not answer. Check the status-link delivery, not the reply quality.

events.subject: Re-cut tool is in
events.body: Broadcast: the re-cut mould passed first shot. Production restarts. Band narrows by two weeks.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Narrow the band on the status page and push the update. Good news moves the band too. Watch whether refund requests fall in the following week and log the delta from the baseline.

events.subject: Customs
events.body: Will I be charged import duty in Australia? Last hardware campaign hit me with an $80 entry fee plus $600 of duty and nobody warned me.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Duty shock is a real post-delivery refund driver. Put the regional duty note on the status page for the AU/EU cohorts rather than answering it 300 times.

events.subject: Still in
events.body: Good update. Still in.
events.expectedOperatorAction: Log CSAT. Use the 30-day outcome ledger to compute the actual reply-time delta versus the day-0 baseline - and state the assumptions inline when reporting it.

personas.withoutTideover: Two people in a shared Gmail inbox, a Google Sheet exported from the pledge manager, and the Kickstarter comment wall. At 18,400 backers, a delay post generates a wave they physically cannot answer one at a time. Using the merchant-sourced figure of 5-10 minutes per WISMO ticket and a delay-week volume of 120-260 tickets/day, the reply load runs 10-43 person-hours/day against a 2-person team - a SIMULATED formula-based estimate from stated assumptions, not a measured result. What actually happens: they stop answering individually, the comment wall becomes the only channel, morale drops, the next update gets delayed because nobody wants to face the thread, and the refund/chargeback tail is discovered at the bank rather than in the inbox.

personas.name: Devon Marsh
personas.story: We funded a 400-page TTRPG hardback on Kickstarter and moved everyone into BackerKit for the pledge manager and late pledges, which is what everyone told us to do. The print run is fine. What is not fine is that our BackerKit exports are three different files and none of them contains everything, so we are reconciling by hand at midnight. Backers are now asking why we cannot even tell them what they ordered.
personas.dataReceived: BackerKit exports. No single BackerKit export carries email + money + date + tier together. The Fulfillment export (the obvious one to grab) is email + SKUs with NO money, so every row would hit Tideover's $50 order-value floor - which pegs ltvCents at $50 against the hardcoded $500 high tier, meaning the gift/save gate never fires for anyone. The Collected Revenue export has backer ID, email, transaction ID, date, amount, source - but no reward tier and no name. Only the Custom Export builder gets close: Order ID, Order Status, charge amount, pledge amount, reward title + price, timestamp of payment. Even then, firstName is not in the Custom Export field list, so drafts open 'Hi dana87' from the email local-part. No estimated-delivery column on any export, so disclosedEta is undefined.

personas.withoutTideover: Three BackerKit exports reconciled by hand in Excel, a shared support@ inbox, and a Discord where the loudest backers set the mood. The reconciliation is the tax: nothing in BackerKit gives money, name, tier, and date in one file, so answering 'what did I order and when does it ship' means joining two spreadsheets on backer ID. At 2,600 backers with two cohorts on different clocks, and 15-25 tickets/day in a delay week at 5-10 min each, that is 1.3-4.2 hours/day before any reconciliation - a SIMULATED formula-based estimate from stated assumptions, not a measured result. What slips: the late-pledge cohort never gets told they are on a different clock, the $320 deluxe backer waits nine days for a refund answer, and the 'I never got my survey' tickets get treated as wait complaints instead of the mechanical spam-filter problem they are.

personas.dataReceived: Zendesk trigger -> webhook -> Tideover ingest. Tideover receives: ticket.id -> externalId, ticket.title -> subject (there is no ticket.subject in Zendesk), ticket.description -> body, ticket.requester.email -> customerEmail, ticket.created_at_with_timestamp -> createdAt (ISO-8601), ticket.tags. Our template field names are CORRECT here, and this is the only helpdesk where the canonical rail actually fits. THREE LIVE DEFECTS: (1) {{ticket.tags}} renders as a SPACE-SEPARATED STRING, not an array. Our template emits "tags": ["{{ticket.tags}}"] which yields ["presale wismo urgent"] as ONE element, and drop-at-edge does an exact allowed.includes(t) check - so any ticket with 2+ tags is silently 200-'discarded' and never persisted. This merchant routes everything on multi-tag. (2) {{ticket.description}} is the FIRST comment and, per Zendesk's own placeholder reference, includes the requester's name and the comment date as a preamble - so the body we classify and feed the drafter is never the latest customer message. (3) the order_ref placeholder needs a numeric custom-field ID the merchant must look up. NO helpdesk carries money: Zendesk's placeholder reference has zero financial placeholders, so orderValueCents must come from a CSV or it hits the $50 floor.

personas.story: We run group buys. You pay up front, we do a 120-day production cycle with a factory in Shenzhen, and everyone knows the rules going in because this community has done it fifty times. We use Help Scout because it is the only inbox that does not feel like a call centre. So we are forwarding emails and losing people.
personas.dataReceived: THE CANONICAL RAIL DOES NOT WORK HERE. Help Scout webhooks are NOT templatable (fixed v2 Conversation payload) and sign with X-HelpScout-Signature = base64(HMAC-SHA1), while Tideover requires merchant-templated canonical JSON plus X-Tideover-Signature: sha256=<hex>. Riding the shipped ingest rail is impossible without a net-new vendor adapter, a normalizer, and a second signature scheme. WORKAROUND IN PLAY FOR THIS SIM: the merchant forwards Help Scout conversation notifications to their Tideover inbound address (<inboxToken>@in.tideover.app, ADR-0008). That means Tideover receives an EMAIL, not a ticket - and the From header is Help Scout, not the customer, so customerEmail is wrong on every forwarded item unless the parser digs it out of the body. Result: unmatched tickets -> placeholder customer, presale:unmatched tag, NO draft, and getQueue skips order-less tickets, so they are invisible in the cockpit. Money comes from a CSV of group-buy orders or not at all. Help Scout tags are OBJECTS, not strings, so any tag-based filtering built for the string rail misreads them.

personas.name: Jamie Sorensen
personas.story: We are fulfilling our second game while our third is funding, which everybody told us not to do and which we did anyway because the studio does not eat otherwise. So half my inbox is people who paid eighteen months ago and want to know where their box is, and the other half is people who paid last week and are watching how we answer the first half before they decide whether to trust us.
personas.dataReceived: Two Kickstarter CSV imports into ONE merchant record: Campaign A (Deepwater, 2,400 backers, day 78 of fulfilment) and Campaign B (Saltmarsh, 900 early backers, day 4). Tideover receives per row: email, firstName, orderValueCents, sourceKey->importKey, group. CRITICAL STRUCTURAL PROBLEM: campaignName/wave are NEVER MAPPED at import - the field does not survive - so both campaigns land in one undifferentiated population with wildly different fulfillmentStart dates (74 days apart) and there is no first-class cohort key to separate them. The merchant.stages day-bands are a single set applied to both, so Campaign B backers on day 4 are being scored against a stage model built for Campaign A. productionStage is derived at import from elapsed days vs stages[].dayBand and is a SNAPSHOT that nothing advances, so it goes stale by exactly the number of days since import - which on a two-campaign record means one cohort's stage is drifting while the other's is meaningless. About 640 people are backers of BOTH campaigns and appear as two orders with two clocks under one email.

personas.dataReceived: Shopify store plus a Gorgias helpdesk. Assume the Gorgias webhook is connected. Per ticket Tideover receives ONLY the documented Gorgias variables: ticket.id -> externalId, ticket.subject -> subject, ticket.customer.email -> customerEmail, ticket.created_datetime -> createdAt. body/tags/order_ref come from template variables that appear in NO documented Gorgias list, so they are guesses that can render empty - and CanonicalIngestSchema has no .min(1) on body, so an empty body ingests silently, classifies as 'other'/'calm', and buries a chargeback threat at the bottom of the risk queue. Gorgias offers only a static header or OAuth2, never per-request HMAC, so X-Tideover-Signature cannot be produced and every ticket 401s once DEMO_MODE=false. Shopify is NOT WIRED (zero code), so the fields that would make this persona's money real - Customer.amountSpent, Order.totalPriceSet, Order.createdAt - are unavailable; order value and dates come from a CSV export or hit the $50 floor. Even if Shopify were wired, it has NO estimated-delivery field and NO production-stage concept on Order, so it would still not supply a wait clock.

personas.withoutTideover: Gorgias with three agents, Shopify admin, a shipping-block spreadsheet, and a community forum that is louder than all of them. The support team writes the same three paragraphs a hundred times a day because there is nothing to paste: no tracking number exists for another four months, and the block spreadsheet is the only source of truth. At 90-160 tickets/day in the month after a six-month slip, at 5-10 minutes each, the load is 7.5-26 person-hours/day against three seats - a SIMULATED formula-based estimate from stated assumptions, not a measured result. What slips: refund requests wait 15-20 days for a first reply, which is the grievance that produces the chargeback, the BBB complaint, and the review; the $500 Pro upgrade sits in the WISMO queue for nine days; the twelve-unit maker-space partner is indistinguishable from a single $799 order; and the block logic that would defuse the fairness anger is never published because nobody has time to write it down.
